intent: To illustrate the low life expectancy of Bangladesh relative to the USA and South Korea, highlighting the country's development challenges.

units.meaning: Bangladesh has the lowest life expectancy among the three entities, at 47 years.

basis.note: Comparison value showing Bangladesh is lower
Comparison value showing Bangladesh is lower

accepted_routes: Bangladesh's life expectancy was 47 years, the lowest of the three.
At 47 years, Bangladesh ranked below USA and South Korea.
Bangladesh had the shortest life-expectancy bar at about 47 years.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Show three labeled bars and make Bangladesh's bar the shortest, with the 47-year value visible or annotated.
units.temporal_anchor: the life-expectancy clause ('Life expectancy was around 45')
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly state Bangladesh's absolute life expectancy (47), or is its lowest position enough?

units.meaning: USA has the highest life expectancy at 71 years, and South Korea is at 52 years.
accepted_routes: USA had the highest life expectancy at 71 years.
South Korea's life expectancy was 52 years.
USA at 71 and South Korea at 52 years were both above Bangladesh.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Show USA's bar as the highest with 71 visible or annotated, and South Korea's bar or value at 52 visible.
units.temporal_anchor: the life-expectancy clause ('Life expectancy was around 45')
units.reviewer_question: Must both USA and South Korea values be shown, or is only the USA comparison required?

units.meaning: The life-expectancy order is USA (71) > South Korea (52) > Bangladesh (47).
accepted_routes: The order was USA first, South Korea second, Bangladesh last.
Life expectancy fell from 71 in the USA to 52 in South Korea to 47 in Bangladesh.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Show all three bars in descending order USA > South Korea > Bangladesh, with values or clear ordering labels.
units.temporal_anchor: the life-expectancy clause ('Life expectancy was around 45')
units.reviewer_question: Is the full ordering USA > South Korea > Bangladesh required, or only Bangladesh's bottom rank?

units.meaning: Bangladesh trails the USA by 24 years and South Korea by 5 years.

basis.note: Used to compute gap to Bangladesh
Used to compute gap to Bangladesh
Compared against USA and South Korea

accepted_routes: Bangladesh was 24 years below the USA.
South Korea was 5 years above Bangladesh.
Bangladesh trailed South Korea by 5 years.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Show gap/difference annotations or a clear visual comparison between Bangladesh and USA (24 years) and between Bangladesh and South Korea (5 years).
units.temporal_anchor: the life-expectancy clause ('Life expectancy was around 45')
units.reviewer_question: Are explicit year gaps (24 vs USA, 5 vs South Korea) required, or is visual ordering sufficient?

units.meaning: Bangladesh's life expectancy is about 66.2% of the USA's and about 90.4% of South Korea's.
accepted_routes: Bangladesh's life expectancy was about 66% of the USA's.
Bangladesh reached about 90% of South Korea's life expectancy.
Compared with USA, Bangladesh was at roughly two-thirds (47/71 ≈ 66%).
Compared with South Korea, Bangladesh was at about nine-tenths (47/52 ≈ 90%).
units.visual_evidence_rule: Show ratio/percentage annotations comparing Bangladesh to USA (≈66%) and to South Korea (≈90%), or an equivalent relative bar-length comparison.
units.temporal_anchor: the life-expectancy clause ('Life expectancy was around 45')
units.reviewer_question: Are ratio/share comparisons (≈66% of USA, ≈90% of South Korea) required or optional?

optional_valid: Use the table's relative_value bar lengths: USA 0.8875, South Korea 0.6500, Bangladesh 0.5875.
Mention that South Korea is also below the USA by 19 years (71 - 52 = 19).
Mention that USA's life expectancy is about 1.51 times Bangladesh's (71/47 ≈ 1.51).
unsupported_to_avoid: Using the narration's 'around 45' as the charted Bangladesh value instead of the table's 47.
Claiming Bangladesh had the lowest life expectancy in the world; the table only compares three entities.
Causal claims such as low life expectancy being caused by illiteracy, poverty, or per capita income.
Using the literacy value 'one in five' or per capita income claims not present in the table.
Treating relative_value 0.5875 as Bangladesh's share of the USA rather than as the table's own relative measure.
notes: The table gives life expectancy values in years; relative_value is available but not used as a required unit because its denominator is not explicit. Required units focus on Bangladesh's bottom value, the three-country order, and explicit gaps.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
